summary.intent: Execute all 8 plans in phase 60 (IPNS Verification Cross-Layer Closeout) using the GSD wave-based executor, then run the ship-phase workflow to push a PR, pass CI, and resolve reviews.
summary.outcome: All 7 code plans executed and local gates pass (351 Rust, 252 sdk-core, 172 API jest, 89/89 SDK E2E); a ship-blocking regression in 60-05 was caught by the SDK E2E gate and fixed before shipping. 60-08 (staging cutover) is paused at a human-action checkpoint. The PR had not been opened by end of session due to 1Password signing wedge.

repo: Ed25519 IPNS records do NOT embed pubKey in the record protobuf bytes — the public key lives in the IPNS name (k51…). The API must supply it from the separate FolderIpns.publicKey DB column, not parse it from the network record.

60-05's removal of withCachedPublicKey and the equal-seq enrich in resolveRecord was based on a false assumption ('pubKey is already embedded in the signed record'). This broke the publish→resolve round-trip for all Ed25519 records.
The API resolveRecord must return the DB signed record (not the bare network result) on equal-or-higher sequence so the strict client receives all sig fields needed for verifyIpnsRecordSignature.
Unit tests for ipns.service.spec.ts masked the pubKey regression by mocking parseIpnsRecord to include pubKey — a behavior that never occurs for real Ed25519 records.
Phase 60 requires a local DB wipe before running SDK E2E tests in strict mode; pre-strict DB records cause failures distinct from the regression caught here.
Cargo.lock must be committed after any Cargo.toml dependency change or --locked CI breaks; Wave 1 executor added ciborium+cipherbox-core to api-client but didn't commit the lockfile.
GSD executor commit helper has a known false-negative: reports commit_failed while the commit actually lands — always verify with git log --oneline -1.

Sequential gsd-executor subagents on the feature branch were chosen over worktree isolation because the worktree path/branch manifest is not reliably exposed for merge-back, especially for a security-critical phase.

Cross-layer parity gap: Rust resolveIpnsRecord fail-closes on absent Validity via .ok_or_else(); TS resolveIpnsRecord only enforced EOL when Validity was already a Uint8Array, silently accepting records with no Validity field.
SDK E2E harness generates unique accounts per run (email with Date.now()), so failures cannot be attributed to stale-data collisions — any failure is a real regression.

code.finding: resolveRecord returned the bare network result (from parseIpnsRecordBytes) on equal-seq, stripping sig fields. Must return the DB cachedResult to preserve signatureV2/data/pubKey for the strict client.
parseCachedRecord needed a publicKey parameter to supply pubKey from the FolderIpns.publicKey column; without it, the returned record has no pubKey field and the strict client throws fail-closed.

Strict resolve requires pubKey in the API response and verifies deriveIpnsName(pubKey) === ipnsName. The else branch (all three sig fields absent) throws the fail-closed error that caused 28/89 SDK E2E failures.
Absent Validity field was not fail-closed — EOL enforcement only ran when Validity was already a Uint8Array. Fix: throw if Validity is missing, mirroring crates/api-client/src/ipns.rs:114-117.

The D-06 unit test mocked parseIpnsRecord to return pubKey, which real Ed25519 records never do. This masked the regression. Test was rewritten to assert correct verifiable-record behavior without pubKey in the network mock.
Rust fail-closes on absent Validity via .ok_or_else() — the reference implementation for the TS parity fix.

workflow: The SDK E2E suite is the only gate that exercises the real client→API IPNS publish→resolve round-trip. Unit suites mock the boundary and miss integration regressions; this gate caught a 28/89 break (matching the Phase 51 pattern of 48/89).

1Password SSH signing agent wedges after rapid sequential commits (op-ssh-sign: failed to fill whole buffer). Recovery: quit and reopen 1Password desktop app or toggle Settings → Developer → SSH agent off/on.
Running SDK E2E while blocked on signing is a valid parallel strategy — the gate can run and confirm green before the commit is possible.

Commitlint's subject-no-parens rule rejects any parenthetical in the commit subject description (not just the scope). A trailing (D-07) suffix on a feat commit violates it and must be stripped before PR open.
Wave executors can miss ticking their own ROADMAP checkbox and leave stale SUMMARY footers — spot-check both after each wave and reconcile manually.
cargo test --workspace is the authoritative local Rust gate before shipping; cargo check per-crate is sufficient as a wave integration gate during execution.

friction: 1Password SSH signing agent wedged after ~28 rapid commits (op-ssh-sign: failed to fill whole buffer), blocking all further commits until the user restarted the app. No automated recovery path.
GSD commit helper false-negative: reports commit_failed on success — caused false alarm and wasted a verification round-trip after every commit.
Wave 1 executor added Cargo.toml dependencies (ciborium, cipherbox-core) but never committed Cargo.lock — would have caused a latent --locked CI break had it not been caught manually.
60-06's executor did not tick its own ROADMAP checkbox — required a separate reconciliation commit.
60-01-SUMMARY.md had a stale footer appended after the plan's commit (claimed verify.rs FOUND after 60-04 deleted it) — had to be reverted before the SUMMARY was accurate.

60-05's unit test actively codified the buggy resolve behavior (mocking pubKey into the network record), meaning the regression shipped undetected through all unit suites and was only caught at SDK E2E.
